newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ex-Amsterdam air cargo busy, surcharge a talking point.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Amsterdam air cargo busy, surcharge a talking point.

text.p: The air cargo market from Amsterdam to Asia and the Middle East is very busy and carriers are reporting that aircraft to all destinations are full, a Reuters survey showed.
Although much talk surrounds the fuel surcharge there do not seem to be many moves towards dropping it, industry sources said.

Delta Air Lines dropped its fuel surcharge last week but as yet, despite rumours otherwise no other carries have withdrawn the charge. At Schiphol, there is much speculation concerning Lufthansa which is expected to make an announcement soon concerning the charge.
At Schiphol, Northern Asian destinations such as Japan and Korea are particularly busy, and they are expected to continue to be very active in the coming weeks.

Pim de Goederen, cargo manager of Japan Airlines, said Japan is especially busy because of the consumption tax increases being introduced in Japan in the beginning of April. The tax is rising by two percent to five percent on April 1.
For many Japanese companies it is also the end of their fiscal year so there is also a slight surge as companies import goods before then, he added.

Demand has been so strong that the Japanese carrier has added some extra flights out of its European destinations. JAL has Boeing 747-200 freighter flight's from Paris, Frankfurt and London. Ex-Amsterdam, the carrier operates MD-11 passenger flights.
Yields are much better now, said de Goederen. The carrier was one of the only airlines not to apply a fuel surcharge but JAL increased its rates from January 1.
He added that the ex-Amsterdam market may see a slight slow- down in April and May following the boom created because of the Japanese VAT increase.
A spokesman for all-cargo carrier, Nippon Cargo Airlines, said it too was experiencing more demand because of the tax increase and it was also experiencing full loads.
The carrier would always like to see more capacity out of the Netherlands into Japan but it is restricted because Narita Airport is so congested the carrier cannot get any more slots.
The Japanese cargo rate appears to be holding at around 4.50 guilders per kilo at the moment.
Korea is also very busy. Mike Zimmerman, cargo manager of Korean Air Lines in Amsterdam, said: "Aircraft are full, more than full. It is very busy currently."
KAL has been so busy that it has also brought in more capacity. A second 747-200 freighter was brought into Amsterdam last week.
The second freighter was due to be introduced last year but this was postponed. The main reason for the delay was because volume levels from Korea to Amsterdam were weak.
Seoul-headquartered, Korean, was worried that introducing the extra freighter last year would lead to too much capacity.
The introduction of a freighter in the winter season may have led to too much capacity ex-Amsterdam and this may lead to a break down of the rates levels, said Zimmerman.
The second freighter's arrival had been negotiated since the Dutch-Korean bilateral talks which took place in February last year.
Rates ex-Amsterdam are currently stable and relatively healthy hovering between 4-4.10 guilders.
Taiwan is another Asian destination experiencing high demand and Hans Lin, European general manager of Taiwanese carrier, EVA Air, said volumes are up on this time last year.
EVA Air has decided to transfer part of its freighter service from Schiphol to Brussels Airport, said Lin.
Eva will start a twice-weekly freighter service into Brussels on May 10 in addition to a weekly freighter service into Schiphol.
Currently it operates a three-times-a-week freighter service into the Dutch airport with an MD-11 freighter, he added.
As well as moving the two freighter services, Eva will begin an MD-11 passenger service into Amsterdam, on a three-times-a-week basis from May 9.
"We will now have six flights a week into the Benelux to offer shippers and the passenger flights will give us around 12 tonnes a flight from Amsterdam as well as the freighter," he added.
EVA is setting up an office at Brussels Airport as this will be the first time the carrier has operated into Belgium.
The operator still has the fuel surcharge in place and recently, on March 15, EVA increased its rates by around five percent.
Early January was a struggle in the Hong Kong market, said Air Hong Kong's European general manager, Marcel Buelens, but the Benelux-Hong Kong market has been very busy since mid- February, he added.
However, weak volumes in the early part of the year, led the carrier to reduce its capacity from six to four B747-200 freighter flights a week out of the Benelux.

"We felt this would stabilise the market as the rates were under severe pressure in the first part of the year. Currently the market is less aggressive rates-wise," he said. But the carrier will increase its flights again in May.
Hong Kong is more busy than many other Asian destinations, he said, perhaps because of the Chinese taking over in July, he speculated.
The market is expected to get even busier soon as the summer fashions head for Hong Kong from Europe. Clothes from Italy and shoes from Spain and Switzerland are the major exports.

Air Hong Kong increased its rates from March 1 and it intends to increase them again in September. "It is our policy to increase the rates twice a year with plenty of notice because we are aiming to build a long-term relationship with our customers," said Buelens.
Cargolux'S cargo manager in the Netherlands, Peter Schoute, said the market is currently active on all destinations.
"For Cargolux the first three months of the year were very good, in fact we have had problems getting rid of some backlogs."
"It is very strong at the moment, all of our flights are booked nearly two and a half weeks in advance," Schoute stated.

In April, the Asian market receives a further boost when the flower bulb season out of the Netherlands really gets underway. Japan is expected to be even busier during this season. In addition the vegetable market to the U.S. gets under way.
Schoute said the Middle East market is perhaps more stable than Asia but this market is also doing very well.
Bert van der Velde of Winfo World Freight said the Middle Eastern market is particularly busy and March 1997 has proved busier than this time last year.
Tijn Middendorp, Middle East trade director of MSAS, said destinations in the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Kuwait are fairly active at the moment but Saudi Arabia is quiet currently.
Chickens and hatching eggs are major exports to many Middle East destinations, he added.

Over the last month Polar Air's new twice-weekly freighter service has brought more capacity to the Middle East as the service calls into Dubai before flying on to India. And in May, EVA Air begins a three-times-weekly passenger service between Taipei and Amsterdam which also calls at Dubai.
Rates to Dubai are very variable at the moment due to the new competition. Several sources said cargo rates ex-Amsterdam to Dubai can vary from 1.50 to 1.80 guilders.
